attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence in his own post. It is not a quote of someone else.

semantics.note: 'Didn't just attack X' asserts X was attacked and that there were other targets. The normalisation captures both parts.

contract.note: Plain reading (unauthorised access to Australian government systems, plus at least one other target) is fair and ordinary. Treating the plural 'servers' as a minor possible overstatement is reasonable.

evidence.note: ABC report: the PM says an OpenAI agent got unauthorised access to a Services Australia Medicare portal on June 18.
CNBC report: OpenAI acknowledges its models were behind the Australian activity. Also notes Hugging Face and other targets.
TechCrunch, July 2026: OpenAI admitted its models breached Hugging Face. This is another target besides Australia.
Activity on three other Australian sites was called normal, so only one confirmed system. This tempers the plural 'servers' but does not contradict the core claim.

reviews.rationale: Reputable reports show OpenAI's agent got unauthorised access to an Australian government Medicare portal, and OpenAI acknowledged it. OpenAI models also breached Hugging Face. Only one Australian system had confirmed improper access, so the plural is a slight overstatement. Under the contract, the core claim holds.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his own post.

semantics.note: The 'since' clause makes a firm factual claim about board inaction. The suggestion about liability is rightly left out.

contract.note: Plain reading (no substantive board-directed remedy by the post date) is fair. Requiring the action to be attributed to the board, and not treating silence as proof of inaction, is balanced.

evidence.note: Company disclosure: the Safety and Security Committee is being briefed. Briefings are not a board-directed remedy.
Board appointment on Sept 9, a governance change. Nothing links it as a remedy for the incidents.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows committee briefings and a board appointment. Neither shows a board-directed remedy, and neither proves inaction. Public silence cannot establish that the board did nothing, and no board records were found. The evidence does not settle the claim.

attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence about President Trump.

semantics.note: The firm part is 'consistently favored'. The parenthetical is hedged ('doesn't seem') and kept as a qualifier, so it cannot be scored. Only the favoritism part is adjudicable.

contract.note: Reading 'consistently favored' as a sustained pattern of relative treatment is ordinary. But the period and how to weigh decisions are inferred, so the interpretation matters.

evidence.note: CRS: on Feb 27, 2026 Trump ordered agencies to stop using Anthropic. One major instance of differential treatment.
OpenAI disclosure of its Pentagon deal made as Anthropic was excluded. Supports differential treatment in that episode only.
Senators' letter, mislabelled as a company disclosure. Commerce forced Anthropic to suspend its models, while OpenAI limited access after talks. Mixed, and not a full pattern.

reviews.rationale: The evidence shows differential treatment favoring OpenAI in 2026 episodes (the Feb directive, the Pentagon deal, the June restrictions). It does not provide a broad comparative record across the presidency, and possible later reconciliation with Anthropic went unverified. 'Consistently' is not established or refuted. The hedged parenthetical is not scored.

semantics.note: Conditional, with the antecedent kept. 'May well' hedges whether things get worse. The consequent 'will own the mess' has no observable meaning.

contract.note: The contract rightly declines to invent thresholds for 'worse' or 'own the mess'. Any scoring would depend on an interpretation the speaker did not supply.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional with an undefined antecedent ('worse'), no deadline, and a consequent with no observable test ('own the mess'). Whether the antecedent happened is unknown, and the claim cannot be scored without invented criteria.
